title: Rome: Paul’s Arrival & Imperial Context
subtitle: Via Appia approach, city-level ministry, and Revelation interpretation kept distinct
summary: Follow the secure broad approach from Puteoli toward Rome, orient to the imperial city, and keep Paul’s rented lodging and Revelation’s symbolic Babylon separate from any invented terrestrial point.
disclaimer: Rome is securely located, while Paul’s rented lodging and Three Taverns remain unpinned. The Appii Forum coordinate is approximate. Revelation’s “Babylon the Great” remains a coordinate-free visionary entity even where Rome is judged a strong first-century interpretive referent.

options.label: Imperial Rome
options.summary: Rome is a securely identified historical city and imperial capital.
options.rationale: The city can be mapped confidently even when individual biblical addresses cannot.
options.objections: No complete first-century city model or specific Pauline residence is claimed.

options.label: Paul’s arrival
options.summary: Acts gives a secure sequence through Puteoli and toward Rome; the exact overland track and Three Taverns coordinate are not fully recoverable.
options.rationale: Puteoli and the approximate Appii Forum can illustrate the approach without drawing an exact road trace.
options.objections: Three Taverns and Paul’s rented lodging remain unpinned, and no street-by-street itinerary is asserted.

camera.note: Regional teaching camera for the Bay of Naples-to-Rome approach; not an exact route reconstruction.

options.label: Revelation & Rome
options.summary: Many interpreters regard Rome as the primary first-century referent for Revelation’s Babylon imagery, without reducing the symbol to one mapped city.
options.rationale: Imperial power, commerce, and seven-hill imagery make Rome a strong interpretive context.
options.objections: “Babylon the Great” remains a visionary/symbolic entity with no terrestrial coordinates and may deliberately exceed any single historical referent.

camera.note: Shows historical Rome only; it does not assign coordinates to Babylon the Great.

hotspots.label: Rome
hotspots.summary: Secure imperial city and the city-level destination of Acts 28.

whyShown.evidence: Rome is an established historical and archaeological city.
whyShown.inference: It securely anchors Paul’s final Acts destination and wider imperial context.
whyShown.alternatives: Paul’s rented lodging is not assigned to any excavated building.

hotspots.label: Puteoli
hotspots.summary: Securely identified Bay of Naples port where Acts says Paul stayed seven days before continuing toward Rome.

whyShown.evidence: Ancient Puteoli is securely identified with Pozzuoli.
whyShown.inference: It provides a reliable anchor for the final Italian phase of Acts 28.
whyShown.alternatives: The onward overland route is represented only broadly until a verified road dataset is integrated.

hotspots.label: Forum of Appius / Appii Forum
hotspots.summary: Approximate atlas location on the Appian corridor where believers met Paul according to Acts 28.

whyShown.evidence: Acts names the Forum of Appius and the broader Appian approach is historically real.
whyShown.inference: The atlas coordinate is approximate and suitable for regional orientation.
whyShown.alternatives: Three Taverns remains unpinned and no exact Paul-on-the-road coordinate is supplied.
